The official ACP server (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-acp`) is automation-only: "},{"id":"p7s3","text":"it creates fresh sessions but cannot load / list / resume / fork existing ones, so it cannot power a"},{"id":"p7s4","text":" full desktop console."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"That is why **DeepSeek Harness App builds on the official web UI instead of reinventing it**: we add"},{"id":"p8s2","text":" only what a browser cannot — a native shell, tray residency, and desktop integrations."},{"id":"p9s1","text":"## Why this is different from fork-based shells"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"Some desktop clients fork or vendor the DeepSeek Harness source and ship their own “core”. That make"},{"id":"p10s2","text":"s the package heavier, can drift from upstream, and often freezes the core until the shell project u"},{"id":"p10s3","text":"pdates it. dsh-app does the opposite:"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"|  | Fork/vendor-based shells | dsh-app |"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"| **Core** | Bundle or fork the dsh codebase, often with modified internals | Use the official local"},{"id":"p12s2","text":" `@deepseek-ai/dsh` CLI from npm — no fork, no rewrite |
| **Update path** | Wait for the shell main"},{"id":"p12s3","text":"tainer to merge upstream changes | Sync official dsh releases from npm/GitHub Releases; one-click ch"},{"id":"p12s4","text":"eck and upgrade |
| **Independence** | If the shell stops being maintained, the bundled core can be "},{"id":"p12s5","text":"stuck | dsh core is official and can always be upgraded independently of this App |
| **Footprint** "},{"id":"p12s6","text":"| Often Electron + copied/duplicated web UI | Lightweight Tauri native shell + official web UI; dsh "},{"id":"p12s7","text":"runs from your local installation |
| **Browser access** | The shell may own/alter the only running "},{"id":"p12s8","text":"server or fork the UI | App starts or reuses the standard local dsh web — the same service stays rea"},{"id":"p12s9","text":"chable in your browser |"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"Practical highlights:"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"- **Automatic Node / CLI detection** — the startup wizard checks Node, npm, and dsh in order; it fin"},{"id":"p14s2","text":"ds dsh from `DSH_BIN` → npm global → PATH → common install dirs, and reports versions and paths.
- *"},{"id":"p14s3","text":"*One-click install / upgrade** — missing Node? The app downloads an official managed Node into `~/.d"},{"id":"p14s4","text":"sh-app/node` (no admin). Missing dsh? It installs `@deepseek-ai/dsh` through npm automatically (mirr"},{"id":"p14s5","text":"or-aware in Chinese environments). Both App and dsh CLI can be checked and upgraded from the setting"},{"id":"p14s6","text":"s page.
- **Automatic start/stop management** — on launch the App reuses a bridge-enabled `dsh web` "},{"id":"p14s7","text":"at `127.0.0.1:3080`, or starts its own `dsh --profile dsh-app --port 0`; on quit it cleans up the wh"},{"id":"p14s8","text":"ole process tree. Your manually started plain `dsh web` is left untouched, and launching the App doe"},{"id":"p14s9","text":"s not block browser access.
